meaning: A short message sent over wires and written out at the other end. A messenger then brought it to the door.
clues: It was a short message sent by wire, then delivered by hand.
You paid by the word, so people kept them very short.
The word STOP was used where a period would go.
It started out as Morse code tapped out on a telegraph.
It has eight letters and starts with T. Western Union stopped sending them in 2006.
assumes: A fax machine sends a copy of a whole page
A postcard travels by mail on paper

decoys.meaning: A machine that scans a paper page and sends a copy over a phone line. Another machine prints the copy.
A card you write on and mail without an envelope.
A machine with a keyboard that presses letters onto paper, one key at a time.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Back in my day, we paid by the word, so we wrote like this: ARRIVING TUESDAY STOP. Short and sweet.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Today's version: a text message. Same idea, short and fast, but you can use as many words as you like.
